## Report on `region.fasta` (sequence `locus_005`)

**Basic facts**
- Length: **3,000 bp** (single record).
- Base composition is close to uniform: A 785 (26.2%), T 784 (26.1%), C 718 (23.9%), G 713 (23.8%); overall **GC = 47.7%**. No unusual skew.

**Main notable feature — a tandem repeat (minisatellite/VNTR-like array)**
- A **20-bp unit, `TACTTACATGTGCGTAAGGT`, is present as 4 perfect head-to-tail copies**, i.e. an 80-bp perfect tandem array at **positions 1855–1934** (1-based, inclusive) on the given strand:

```
1855 TACTTACATGTGCGTAAGGT
1875 TACTTACATGTGCGTAAGGT
1895 TACTTACATGTGCGTAAGGT
1915 TACTTACATGTGCGTAAGGT
```
- The unit is AT-biased (40% GC), in contrast to the 47.7% average of the region. The array is not flanked by partial copies — the 5′ flank (`…AACCATACT`, 1835–1854) and 3′ flank (`GCTGCAGC…`, 1935–1954) show no extension of the motif, so the array appears as a clean, isolated 4-copy tract.
- Shorter sub-motifs of this array (e.g. `TTACATGTGCGTAAGGT`, `TACATGTGCGTAAGG`) also occur 4× at the same positions; a 17-bp or 15-bp repeat unit is an equally valid description of the same tract.

**Features that do *not* stand out**
- **No convincing protein-coding content.** The longest open reading frame in either strand is only **53 codons** (positions 1239–1399, +strand); all other ORFs ≥30 codons are 30–52 codons. There is no long ORF, which argues against this being a normal gene body (it looks non-coding / intergenic-like).
- **No other repeats or secondary structures.** A scan for tandem motifs of 3–20 bp (≥3 copies) found only the array above, plus trivial mono-/dinucleotide runs. Scanning for inverted repeats/palindromic stems found nothing longer than a 10-bp stem (positions 1620 and 1804), i.e. no likely hairpin/terminator-type structure. No large internal duplications (no 25-mer occurs anywhere except within the 1855–1934 array).
- Minor low-complexity only: homopolymer tracts `T6` at 1661–1666 and `C6` at 2784–2789.
- Modest local GC variation: the most GC-rich windows are **801–900 and 901–1000 (61% GC each)**; the most AT-rich is **1801–1900 (34%)**, which is due to the repeat array described above. Nothing else lies outside roughly 40–61% GC.

**Summary**
The only clearly notable, non-random feature in this 3 kb region is a perfect 4-copy tandem repeat array of a 20-bp unit at **1855–1934** (a short VNTR/minisatellite, AT-rich relative to its surroundings). The rest of the sequence shows a near-uniform base composition, no long reading frames, no significant inverted repeats, and only trivial homopolymer/low-complexity runs — consistent with a non-coding region carrying one simple tandem repeat.
